       ⟦B⟧Technical Support⟦/B⟧
[0006] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=1
       
[0007] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧⟦LB⟧⟦/B⟧
[0008] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Revisions⟦/B⟧
[0009] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=1
       
[0010] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Get started with Wrapsody
[0011] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ is a content-based file management solution. Wrapsody allows users to access the latest version of a file on their devices (PC or mobile) anytime from anywhere, regardless of its storage location. Wrapsody helps users easily and quickly share information, promoting effective collaboration within an organization.
[0012] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Introduction to Wrapsody
[0013] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Seamless file version management and sharing⟦/B⟧
[0014] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ automatically checks whether a file is the latest version when it is opened and lets users retrieve the latest version from the server if one is available. When a user uploads the edited file as a new version, it is immediately registered on the Wrapsody server and shared with other users.
[0015] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0016] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Secure file management⟦/B⟧
[0017] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       The file owner can grant specific users View and Revise permissions. Users without these permissions cannot access the file, which helps prevent unauthorized changes or damage.
[0018] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0019] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Auto backup and version management⟦/B⟧
[0020] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A checked-in Wrapsody file is automatically backed up to the server along with its version history, allowing users to view the entire lifecycle of the file at a glance.
[0021] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0022] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Analytics on file usage⟦/B⟧
[0023] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody ⟦/B⟧provides visual analytics through the Branch Map and Usage Map, which help users understand file usage patterns and flows. The Branch Map shows how a Wrapsody file is related to its derived Branch files, while the Usage Map shows file usage by department and user. In addition, analytics based on Wrapsody user statistics provides insights into how files are used across the organization.
[0024] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0025] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Real-time communication via file⟦/B⟧
[0026] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Comments left on a Wrapsody file are shared in real time, enabling file-based collaboration without the need for emails or phone calls.
[0027] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0028] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Structural tag management⟦/B⟧
[0029] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Administrators or heads of groups can systemically manage organizational tags using tag groups.
[0030] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0031] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Unrestricted file access⟦/B⟧
[0032] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       The latest version of a file can be accessed anytime and anywhere, not only from PC but also through the Wrapsody mobile app.
[0033] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       
[0034] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Maximizing work efficiency with AI⟦/B⟧
[0035] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       By interacting with the AI librarian, users can quickly and easily find the files they need. In addition, by using AI-powered K-Assistant and Domain K-Master, users can effortlessly obtain reliable knowledge based on internal files accumulated in ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧.
[0036] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦TB⟧
[0037] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Guide set
[0038] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Admin Guide⟦/B⟧: The guide for the administrators and heads of groups in an organization that use ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧. It explains how to manage Wrapsody comprehensively, including how to view group and organization-wide files, handle requests, and manage logs, tags, and licenses.
[0039] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody User Guide (for Windows/Mac)⟦/B⟧: The guide for users of an organization that use ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧. It explains how users can use Wrapsody files through the Wrapsody client or web.
[0040] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody User Guide (for Mobile)⟦/B⟧: The guide for users of an organization that use Wrapsody. It explains how to use the Wrapsody mobile app on mobile devices.
[0041] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Installation Guide⟦/B⟧: The guide for installing the Wrapsody server.
[0042] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Terminology
[0043] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Here are some key terms that will help you understand and use ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧.
[0044] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody file⟦/B⟧: A file that is encrypted by Wrapsody, stored on the Wrapsody server, and whose complete history is tracked
[0045] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapping⟦/B⟧: The process of converting a plain file into a Wrapsody file through encryption
[0046] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Export original⟦/B⟧: The process of exporting the original file by decrypting (unwrapping) a Wrapsody file.
[0047] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Standard supported applications⟦/B⟧: Applications supporting the use and management of Wrapsody files. These include MS Office, Hancom Hangul, Notepad, and Acrobat Reader DC.
[0048] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Non-standard supported applications⟦/B⟧: All applications other than those listed as standard supported applications. These provide partial support for Wrapsody file use and management.
[0049] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧View⟦/B⟧: The process of opening a Wrapsody file in read-only mode to check its content. Users with View or Revise permission can open the file on their PC or view a preview on the website.
[0050] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧View count⟦/B⟧: The number of times that a Wrapsody file has been opened regardless of its mode (Revise, View, or Preview). Views are counted even when a user opens a file after receiving a View request, or while the file’s check-in remains pending.
[0051] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Revise⟦/B⟧: The process of checking out, modifying, and checking in a Wrapsody file. This function is restricted to users with Revise permission.
[0052] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧K-Assistant⟦/B⟧: An abbreviation for Knowledge Assistant. It is an AI-powered feature that analyzes Wrapsody files. When users freely ask K-Assistant questions about files, it provides answers based on AI analysis.
[0053] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧AI Librarian⟦/B⟧: An AI-powered feature that quickly finds the desired Wrapsody files. When users type the criteria for the files they want in a conversional way through AI librarian, it displays the files that meet those criteria in the search results.
[0054] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Domain K-Master⟦/B⟧: An abbreviation for Domain Knowledge Master. An AI-driven knowledge management feature in ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ that helps users effectively handle knowledge within specific domains. It connects and analyzes selected files by topic or business area to provide reliable, context-aware answers with high accuracy.
[0055] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Owner⟦/B⟧: A user who has ownership of a Wrapsody file and can manage its permissions. The user who first creates a Wrapsody file becomes its owner, and this authority can be transferred. An owner has Revise permission by default. 
[0056] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Folder manager⟦/B⟧: The owner of a folder within Wrapsody Drive or Virtual Drive. This user can grant other users permissions such as Read and Write access to the folder. The user who creates a folder becomes its folder owner, and folder ownership can be transferred.
[0057] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody administrator⟦/B⟧:⟦B⟧ ⟦/B⟧A user in charge of the overall Wrapsody management within an organization. Only the administrator is allowed to handle the version delete request, designate the head of the group or other user as an administrator. Also, the administrator can change the owner of multiple files at a time, set or define the tags, or manage the Wrapsody system (license, notification, or client patch settings.)
[0058] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Head of Group⟦/B⟧:⟦B⟧ ⟦/B⟧A user in charge of a group within an organization. A head of group can manage the Wrapsody group files and view the related logs. The administrator can designate a user as the head of group.
[0059] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Usage map⟦/B⟧: A map that shows the usage status of each Wrapsody file by group and by user. Users can view and compare usage data by group and by user.
[0060] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Branch file⟦/B⟧: A Wrapsody file which has been derived from an existing Wrapsody file that has its own version history.
[0061] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Branch Map⟦/B⟧: A map that visualizes all relations among all Branch files derived from a single Wrapsody file.
[0062] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Timeline⟦/B⟧: A feature that displays the history of file usage and management for each version chronologically. Users can manage versions and view the history of each version.
[0063] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody server⟦/B⟧: A server that stores all Wrapsody files and their version information. 
[0064] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody web⟦/B⟧: A web interface designed to help users easily manage and use files stored on the Wrapsody server.
[0065] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody client⟦/B⟧: A program installed on a user’s PC to access and use Wrapsody files.
[0066] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody mobile⟦/B⟧: A mobile app designed to access and view Wrapsody files on mobile devices.
[0067] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive⟦/B⟧: A file repository where users can store and share files. Files within a folder inherit the folder’s permissions, so file permission can be managed simply by managing the folder. Wrapsody Drive web (web interface) and Wrapsody Drive for desktop (accessible through the file explorer) stay synchronized in real time, ensuring that users can access the latest version of a file regardless of where they open it.
[0068] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive file⟦/B⟧: A file stored in Wrapsody Drive, either as a Wrapsody file or a plain file with paths within Wrapsody Drive. It resides in Company, Group, or Personal Drive of Wrapsody Drive, and its usage permissions vary depending on the folder it belongs to.
[0069] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Virtual Drive⟦/B⟧: A file repository where users can store and share files. Files within a folder do not inherit the folder’s permissions but have their own, with access to files can still be managed through the folder. Virtual Drive web (web interface) and Virtual Drive for desktop (accessible through the file explorer) stay synchronized in real time, ensuring that users can access the latest version of a file regardless of where they open it. 
[0070] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Virtual Drive file⟦/B⟧: A file stored in Virtual Drive, either as a Wrapsody file or a plain file with paths within Virtual Drive. It resides in Company, Group, or Personal Drive of Virtual Drive, and its usage permissions can be controlled at the file level regardless of folder location.
[0071] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧: A drive that allows organizational members to access and collaborate by registering folders from Personal or Group Drives as shared targets. Folders that make up the substructure of the drive are called shared folders.
[0072] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Sync ID⟦/B⟧: A unique identifier assigned to every Wrapsody file. Files with the same Sync ID are recognized as a single file on the server, and even if copies exist in multiple locations on a user’s PC, they are always synchronized to the latest version. A Branch file and its original file have different Sync IDs.
[0073] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Offline mode⟦/B⟧: An environment in which a Wrapsody user is not connected to the Internet or the internal network. In offline mode, users can still view or check out files based on their granted permissions, and any changes made are automatically updated to the server when the connection is restored.
[0074] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0

       Install & Uninstall Wrapsody on PC
[0116] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Install client
[0117] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can install the Wrapsody client on your PC using the setup file link or through other distribution tools (PMS or GPO).
[0118] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Make sure that the Wrapsody server is connected to the network before starting installation.
[0119] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click the installation file and run as administrator.
[0120] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Follow the instructions to proceed with the installation.
[0121] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Update client
[0122] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       To update to a higher version, you can install the new version over the existing one without uninstalling the previous version.
[0123] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In the taskbar search field, type “Control Panel”, then select ⟦B⟧Control Panel⟦/B⟧ from the search results.
[0124] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Select ⟦B⟧Programs⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Programs and Features⟦/B⟧.
[0125] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Check the version of the currently installed Wrapsody client (⟦B⟧Fasoo Wrapsody⟦/B⟧).⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: The displayed client program name may vary, such as⟦B⟧ Fasoo WRAPSODY Client⟦/B⟧. If you are unsure of the exact name, look for an item that includes “Wrapsody” in its name and has ⟦B⟧Fasoo Co., Ltd.⟦/B⟧ as the publisher.
[0126] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Verify that the latest installation file provided by your administrator is a higher version than the one you checked above.
[0127] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click the client installation file and run as administrator. 
[0128] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Follow the instructions to proceed with the update. 
[0129] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: The path to ⟦B⟧Programs and Features⟦/B⟧ in Windows may vary depending on the version. For the latest information, ⟦H0⟧refer to the Microsoft Support website⟦/H0⟧.
[0130] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Recover client
[0131] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When an error occurs while using the Wrapsody Client, you can restore the client by running the emergency recovery app.
[0132] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Start⟦/B⟧⟦D0⟧ on the taskbar at the bottom, then click ⟦B⟧All⟦/B⟧.
[0133] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Select ⟦B⟧Fasoo-Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Recovery⟦/B⟧.
[0134] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Follow the instructions to proceed with the emergency recovery.
[0135] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: You can quickly find the app by typing “Wrapsody Recovery” in the taskbar search field.
[0136] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Uninstall client
[0137] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Start⟦/B⟧⟦D0⟧ on the taskbar at the bottom, then click ⟦B⟧All⟦/B⟧.
[0138] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Select ⟦B⟧Fasoo-Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Uninstall⟦/B⟧.
[0139] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Follow the instructions to proceed with the uninstallation.
[0140] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: You can quickly find the app by typing “Wrapsody Uninstall” in the taskbar search field.
[0141] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Log in & Log out
[0142] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can log in to Fasoo Enterprise DRM on your desktop and then use the Wrapsody service. Alternatively, you can also access the service from the website.
[0143] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Log in
[0144] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Web
[0145] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       When you ⟦H0⟧access Wrapsody on the web through the client on your desktop⟦/H0⟧, you’re logged in automatically.
[0146] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦H0⟧Go to Wrapsody on the web⟦/H0⟧.
[0147] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On the login page, enter your ⟦B⟧User ID⟦/B⟧ and ⟦B⟧Password⟦/B⟧, then click ⟦B⟧Log In⟦/B⟧.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: If you select ⟦B⟧Remember user ID⟦/B⟧ at the bottom, your user ID will be saved in the current web browser.
[0148] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Desktop
[0149] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Show hidden icons⟦/B⟧⟦D0⟧ on the right side of the taskbar.
[0150] heading=0 drawings=2 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧DRM Client⟦/B⟧⟦D0⟧, then select ⟦B⟧Log in⟦/B⟧.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: If other Fasoo products are installed, the icon or process may differ. If an icon with blue text on a white background⟦D1⟧ appears, click that icon first, then select ⟦B⟧DRM Client⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Log in⟦/B⟧.

[0176] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody interface
[0177] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody on the web
[0178] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       You can ⟦H0⟧access Wrapsody on the web⟦/H0⟧ to view, use, and manage files easily. Here’s an overview of the Wrapsody web interface.
[0179] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧
[0180] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Navigation menu⟦/B⟧: You can browse internal files by category and manage them efficiently.
[0181] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Documents⟦/B⟧: You can access and work Wrapsody files by category.
[0182] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Management⟦/B⟧: Provides features that make Wrapsody usage more convenient. You can view file usage logs and analytics data, and clean up unnecessary files at once.
[0183] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Drive⟦/B⟧: You can easily access and manage files in Wrapsody Drive and Virtual Drive through the website.
[0184] heading=0 drawings=2 links=3 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Search field⟦/B⟧: You can ⟦H0⟧quickly and easily search for the files you need⟦/H0⟧. By default, both the exact match results for the entered keywords and the AI-powered contextual search results are displayed. Click dropdown⟦D0⟧ to select a search category or choose between ⟦H1⟧AI librarian⟦/H1⟧ and ⟦H2⟧AI-powered search⟦/H2⟧ options. Clicking AI Librarian⟦D1⟧ switches to AI Librarian search mode.
[0185] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧AI Librarian⟦/B⟧: You can find files more quickly and efficiently with AI assistance. Beyond simple keyword searches, AI analyzes context to recommend related files and provide the most relevant results (Displayed only when the AI service is enabled).
[0186] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Notification⟦/B⟧: You can check notifications received in Wrapsody.
[0187] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Profile⟦/B⟧: You can view your account information and adjust personal settings for a more convenient Wrapsody experience.
[0188] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧K-Assistant⟦/B⟧: K-Assistant analyzes Wrapsody files using AI technology. You can ask questions about files and receive quick, accurate answers (Displayed only when the AI service is enabled).
[0189] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Documents > All
[0190] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Displays all files that you have permission to access.
[0191] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦H0⟧Go to Wrapsody on the web⟦/H0⟧.
[0192] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In the left navigation menu, select ⟦B⟧Documents⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧All⟦/B⟧.
[0193] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Refer to the descriptions below for each item.
[0194] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Filename⟦/B⟧: Displays the name of the file registered on the Wrapsody server. This is different from the local filename, which can be edited in the local path. Click Sort⟦D0⟧ to arrange the files in ascending or descending order.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: When sorted in ascending order, files are arranged by numbers first, then English letters (A–Z), and then Korean characters (charlie6–juliet45).
[0195] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       An icon appears before the filename to indicate the file’s status. Refer to the descriptions below.
[0196] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ∙ ⟦D0⟧: A file that you have not read the latest version
[0197] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ∙ ⟦D0⟧: A file currently being checked out by another user
[0198] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ∙ ⟦D0⟧: A file that you have not read after receiving a view request
[0199] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Last revised⟦/B⟧: Displays the date and time when the file was last checked in. Click Sort⟦D0⟧ to arrange files in order of newest to oldest or oldest to newest based on the last checked-in date.
[0200] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Permission⟦/B⟧: Displays the permission you have for the file.
[0201] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧: A file with View permission
[0202] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧: A file with Revise permission
[0203] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧: A file without permission
[0204] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Modifier⟦/B⟧: Displays the user who last checked in the file.
[0205] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Owner⟦/B⟧: Displays the user who has ownership of the file.
[0206] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Use the available ⟦B⟧Search Filters⟦/B⟧ to find the desired files more accurately. Type or select the desired items as described below, then click ⟦B⟧Search⟦/B⟧ to apply the filter.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Click ⟦B⟧Reset⟦/B⟧ to clear all selected filter criteria.
[0207] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Filename⟦/B⟧: Searches for files whose names contain the entered keyword. Type a keyword and press Enter, or click Add⟦D0⟧.
[0208] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Tag⟦/B⟧: When you enter a keyword, existing tags that include the entered text appear in the dropdown list. You can select an existing tag, but new tags cannot be added.
[0209] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Modifier⟦/B⟧: Searches for files last checked in by a specific user. When you type a keyword, a dropdown list appears showing Wrapsody users whose names or IDs include the entered text. You can select the desired user, but cannot add users who do not exist.
[0210] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Owner⟦/B⟧: Searches for files owned by a specific user. When you type a keyword, a dropdown list appears showing Wrapsody users whose names or IDs include the entered text. You can select the desired user, but cannot add users who do not exist.
[0211] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧File type⟦/B⟧: Click the filter to select the desired file type and related options.
[0212] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       File type: ⟦B⟧Word⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Excel⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧PowerPoint⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧PDF⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Hangul⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧TXT⟦/B⟧, and ⟦B⟧OTHERS⟦/B⟧
[0213] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧View plain files only⟦/B⟧: Searches only plain files stored in Wrapsody Drive or Virtual Drive.
[0214] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧View hidden files only⟦/B⟧: Searches only files that have been hidden by the user.
[0215] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Last revised⟦/B⟧: Click the filter to specify⟦B⟧ ⟦/B⟧the date range during which the file was last checked in. The default value is ⟦B⟧All⟦/B⟧, but you can select a predefined option or ⟦B⟧Custom date range⟦/B⟧ to specify the desired period.
[0216] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Include/Exclude unshared files⟦/B⟧: Select whether to include files that only the owner has permission to access.
[0217] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Include/Exclude files accessible to all users⟦/B⟧: Select whether to include files for which all users have View permission.
[0218] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Is opened⟦/B⟧:⟦B⟧ ⟦/B⟧Select ⟦B⟧Opened ⟦/B⟧or ⟦B⟧Unopened ⟦/B⟧based on whether files have been opened by you. The default value is ⟦B⟧All⟦/B⟧.
[0219] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0

[0604] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Key features of Wrapsody
[0605] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       View desired files
[0606] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Find desired files
[0607] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Search files by exact match
[0608] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Displays files whose names, content, or tags exactly match or partially include the entered keyword. Case is ignored for English, but matches are returned only when the word order, spelling, and spacing are identical. This feature is useful when you know the exact file name, tag, or phrase contained in the file.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Example⟦/B⟧: To find a file name “Confidential Document 2023,” only files that have this exact phrase in the name, content, or tag will appear in the search results. Files with typos or altered expressions (e.g., “ConfidentialDocument2023”) will not be displayed.
[0609] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦H0⟧Go to Wrapsody on the web⟦/H0⟧.
[0610] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In the search field at the top of the screen, enter the exact file name or part of the file name you want to find.
[0611] heading=0 drawings=1 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       Press Enter or click Search⟦D0⟧. The search results for the exact phrase are displayed by category (filename, word in content, tag, user), along with the ⟦H0⟧AI Powered search⟦/H0⟧ results at the bottom.

[0669] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       AI Powered search finds files not only by the entered keywords but also by related or similar expressions. It can search even when the word order or sentence structure differs, and find files that contain multiple keywords. This feature is useful for finding highly relevant files.

[0919] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Use & Manage files
[0920] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ helps you manage and use files securely and efficiently. With the Wrapping feature, you can protect your files and share them smoothly with intended users while maintaining security through permission settings. The download, preview, and view functions allow you to easily access and check files, while the version control feature enables you to track changes and restore previous versions. In addition, by using the tag and Branch management features, you can organize file structures systematically and easily identify relationships between related files.
[0921] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Wrapsody features are not supported for Wrapsody files that have been moved to PC Recycle Bin.
[0922] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrap files: convert plain files into Wrapsody files
[0923] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Files newly created on a PC may be automatically wrapped according to the organization’s policy. For files in environments or paths where automatic wrapping does not apply, or for plain files decrypted through Export Original, you can manually wrap the files to convert them into Wrapsody files.
[0924] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, right-click a plain file.
[0925] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Create Wrapsody File⟦/B⟧. The ⟦B⟧Create Wrapsody Document⟦/B⟧ window appears.
[0926] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       In ⟦B⟧Permission Information⟦/B⟧, ⟦H0⟧specify the users to grant permissions to⟦/H0⟧.
[0927] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       In ⟦B⟧Tags⟦/B⟧, you can ⟦H0⟧delete or add tags⟦/H0⟧.
[0928] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Wrap⟦/B⟧. The wrapped file displays the Wrapsody overlay icon(e.g., ⟦D0⟧).
[0929] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrap multiple files at once
[0930] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can wrap multiple files at once to convert them into Wrapsody files.
[0931] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, select multiple plain files and right-click them, or right-click a folder that contains multiple files.
[0932] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Create Multiple Wrapsody Document⟦/B⟧. The ⟦B⟧Create Multiple Wrapsody Document⟦/B⟧ window appears.
[0933] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In ⟦B⟧Details⟦/B⟧, specify the users to grant permissions to and set tags.
[0934] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In ⟦B⟧Options⟦/B⟧, click the checkboxes to select the desired criteria.
[0935] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Include all files in subfolders⟦/B⟧: When a folder is selected, all files in its subfolders are included as wrapping targets.
[0936] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Add the name of the folders containing the target files as new tags⟦/B⟧: The name of the folder containing the target files is added as a tag to the Wrapsody files.
[0937] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Send email notifications for permission granting⟦/B⟧: After wrapping is completed, a permission change email and notification are sent to users who were granted or had permissions withdrawn.
[0938] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Next⟦/B⟧. The list of files to be wrapped appears. You can check ⟦B⟧File path⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Status⟦/B⟧, and ⟦B⟧Details⟦/B⟧ of the files to be converted into Wrapsody files.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: ⟦B⟧Target extensions⟦/B⟧ shown in parentheses on the right side of ⟦B⟧Target Files⟦/B⟧ indicate the supported extensions for wrapping. Files that do not match supported extensions are not displayed in the list.
[0939] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Review the options selected in ⟦B⟧Options⟦/B⟧ and reselect them if needed (optional).
[0940] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Start⟦/B⟧. For wrapped files, ⟦B⟧Status⟦/B⟧ changes from ⟦B⟧Ready⟦/B⟧ to ⟦B⟧Complete⟦/B⟧, and ⟦B⟧Start⟦/B⟧ changes to ⟦B⟧Close⟦/B⟧ at the bottom.

[0942] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0

[0950] heading=0 drawings=2 links=0 trailing_lb=0

[0995] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can modify tags for files with Revise permission.
[0996] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Types of tags in Wrapsody files
[0997] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Tags applied to Wrapsody files are classified into predefined tags provided by the organization and user-defined tags entered manually. Predefined tags are divided into retention policy tags, required tags, and optional tags.
[0998] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Juliet69 kilo90 papa79⟦/B⟧: document charlie82 lima35 foxtrot37 juliet69 juliet25 foxtrot89, document november61 ⟦H0⟧juliet69 papa7 papa63⟦/H0⟧oscar82 golf94 golf98. juliet69 kilo90 charlie82 india44 foxtrot77 papa79.
[0999] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧ Delta31 juliet93 delta31 lima11 papa79.
[1000] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Required tag⟦/B⟧: Tags marked as “⟦B⟧(Required)⟦/B⟧” in the predefined tag list are automatically selected when a file is created and cannot be deleted. You can choose among ⟦B⟧Highly Confidential⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Confidential⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧General⟦/B⟧. The available options may vary depending on internal settings.
[1001] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧: Displayed with green text and a green border.

       ⟦B⟧Optional tag⟦/B⟧: Tags marked as “⟦B⟧(Optional)⟦/B⟧” in the predefined tag list are configured differently based on themes or use cases.

       ⟦D0⟧: Displayed with black text on a gray background.
[1004] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0

       Check out & Check in files: create the latest version
[1126] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       Revise is the process of checking out a file, editing it, and checking it in to create a new version. Only users with ⟦H0⟧Revise permission⟦/H0⟧ can create new versions. The availability of this feature on the web may vary depending on your organization’s internal settings.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Revise for Wrapsody files is also supported in non-standard supported applications. Additional configuration is required to use such applications. Please contact your Wrapsody administrator for assistance.

       Manually check out & check in files
[1187] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Revise refers to the process of modifying a file’s content to create a new version. For certain file types (e.g., dwg, .dxf, .nwd, .nwc), both checking out and checking in must be performed manually. The supported file types may vary depending on internal settings, so please contact your Wrapsody administrator for more details.

[1436] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Create Branch files
[1437] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       A Branch file is a Wrapsody file derived from an existing Wrapsody file that maintains an independent revision history. You can create a Branch file manually, or it may be created automatically when a revision conflict occurs, for example, if another user checks in the file while you are editing it, to protect your changes.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: You can view the overall relationships between linked Branch files in ⟦H0⟧Branch Map⟦/H0⟧.

[1780] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Domain K-Master is an AI-powered knowledge management feature in Wrapsody. It connects knowledge and analyzes content based on selected files organized by topic or business area, providing highly reliable and accurate answers.

       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Within a Domain K-Master, you can create multiple chats. Each created chat retains the full context and Q&A history of previous conversations. Depending on your situation, you can start a new chat or continue an existing one. Chats you create are visible only to you.

[1867] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Key features of Wrapsody Drive
[1868] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody Drive is a virtual drive in Wrapsody that enables users to manage files efficiently within a familiar folder structure. Files inherit permissions from their folders, enabling folder-based file management. Wrapsody Drive is available in two versions: a web version, accessible through Wrapsody on the web, and a desktop version, accessible from the file explorer on your PC. Both versions stay synchronized in real time, ensuring that the latest files are always available wherever you access them.
[1869] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody Drive overview
[1870] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Depending on the Wrapsody Drive management policy, Personal, Group, or Company Drive may not be displayed.
[1871] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Personal Drive⟦/B⟧: A personal workspace for the logged-in user. It is displayed in the format [User name (User ID)] (e.g., Kim Fasoo (fasoo.kim)).
[1872] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Group Drive⟦/B⟧: A workspace for the group or to which the logged-in user belongs. It is displayed under the team or group name. All members of the group can access the Group Drive folder, but access to subfolders depends on each user’s individual permissions.
[1873] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Company Drive⟦/B⟧: A workspace for managing organization-wide files. All members of the organization can access the Company Drive folder, but access to its subfolders depends on each user’s individual permissions.
[1874] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧: A workspace that contains folders shared with the logged-in user. All shared folders the user has access to are displayed here.
[1875] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧My Group⟦/B⟧: When the logged-in user is a direct manager or holds a higher-level permission, they are granted view permission for folders of their managed groups. Even folders without permission can be viewed through the ⟦B⟧My Group⟦/B⟧ drive. In addition, the user can request edit permission for subgroup folders if needed.
[1876] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Access Wrapsody Drive

[1897] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody ⟦/B⟧> ⟦B⟧Drive Properties⟦/B⟧. The Details window of the drive appears.
[1898] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Refer to the descriptions below for each item.
[1899] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧ · ⟦B⟧Group ⟦/B⟧· ⟦B⟧Personal Drive Storage⟦/B⟧: Displays capacity information, including the space allocated to the selected drive and the space currently in use (the total size of the latest versions of all files). It also shows the total size of all versions of all files.
[1900] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Total⟦/B⟧: Displays the storage limit assigned to the drive.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: When ⟦B⟧Total⟦/B⟧ displays ⟦B⟧Unlimited⟦/B⟧, which does not have limit, data for other items is not displayed.
[1901] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Used⟦/B⟧: Displays the amount of space currently occupied by the drive, calculated as the total size of the latest versions of all files.
[1902] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Free⟦/B⟧: Displays the remaining storage space.
[1903] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Total capacity of all file versions⟦/B⟧: Displays the combined size of all versions of all files in the drive.
[1904] heading=0 drawings=2 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Daily storage usage⟦/B⟧: Displays the daily storage usage of the selected drive in a graph. You can click the bar chart⟦D0⟧ or line chart⟦D1⟧ to view the data in the desired graph type. You can also select a specific period during which drive activity occurred to view data for that period at a glance.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: This data is available only on the web.
[1905] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Top 50 files with the largest sizes (Latest version only)⟦/B⟧: Lists the top 50 files in the selected drive with the largest latest-version sizes.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: The ⟦B⟧Top 50 files with the largest sizes (Latest version only)⟦/B⟧ list is displayed only to users who have ownership of the selected drive. For heads of groups, the list appears in Group Drive, while for group members, it appears only in Personal Drive. This data is available only on the web.

[1932] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Manually sync all files in folder in Wrapsody Drive for desktop
[1933] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody Drive for desktop automatically synchronizes with the Wrapsody server in real time, ensuring files are always up to date. Additionally, you can manually synchronize files in the desired path.
[1934] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[1935] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive (W:)⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧.
[1936] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click a file in the drive, then select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Synchronize All Files In Same Folder⟦/B⟧.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Alternatively, click a folder, then select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Synchronize All Subfolders and File⟦/B⟧.
[1937] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       All files in the folder synchronize.
[1938] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Convert files in Wrapsody Drive for desktop to link files
[1939] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In Wrapsody Drive for desktop, you can store files by converting them to link files. Link files occupy zero memory space and function as shortcuts, distinguished by a green overlay mark⟦D0⟧ at the bottom left of the icon.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: To convert a link file back into an original file that occupies storage space, open the file.
[1940] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[1941] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive (W:)⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧.
[1942] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click on a file in the drive and select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Convert to Link File⟦/B⟧.
[1943] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       The file is converted to a link file, marked with the green overlay mark at the bottom left of the icon.
[1944] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Rules for granting permissions in Wrapsody Drive files
[1945] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧All files in Wrapsody Drive inherit the permissions of their parent folders.⟦LB⟧⟦/B⟧Users with Write permission for a folder are granted Revise permission for all files within that folder, while users with Read permission are granted View permission. When a folder’s permissions are modified, the permissions of users who were automatically assigned file permissions through folder inheritance are adjusted accordingly.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: The owner of a file cannot delete or change the folder manager.
[1946] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧The owner of a file can assign user-specific permissions independently from folder permissions.⟦LB⟧⟦/B⟧In addition to permissions automatically granted through folder inheritance, the owner of a file can ⟦H0⟧manually select users to assign file permissions⟦/H0⟧. Even if the folder permissions change, the manually assigned permissions remain unchanged.
[1947] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧When permissions are granted both through folder inheritance and individually, the higher permission is applied.⟦LB⟧⟦/B⟧The higher permissions is displayed in the ⟦B⟧Permission⟦/B⟧ information of the ⟦B⟧Details⟦/B⟧ window.
[1948] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Example⟦/B⟧: If you have Revise permission for a file in a folder where you only have Read permission, you inherit View permission from the folder but retain the higher Revise permission, which is displayed in ⟦B⟧Permission⟦/B⟧ of the ⟦B⟧Details⟦/B⟧ window.
[1949] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Manage files and folders in Wrapsody Drive
[1950] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       When you save a file to Wrapsody Drive or copy or move a folder or file within it, the action follows ⟦H0⟧the file permission granting rules⟦/H0⟧.
[1951] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody Drive Web and Wrapsody Drive for desktop are synchronized in real time, ensuring you can access the latest files from any path.
[1952] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When a file or folder is modified in Shared Drive, the same changes are synchronized with the original file or folder in Personal or Group Drives.
[1953] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Save files to Wrapsody Drive
[1954] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can save files directly to Wrapsody Drive you have viewed or edited on your local PC. Files are saved either as new Wrapsody files or plain files, depending on the Wrapping policy. Files cannot be saved directly to the root folders of Company, Group, Personal, or Shared Drive; they must be saved to subfolders instead.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: If the storage space of Wrapsody Drive is insufficient, new files cannot be saved to that drive. However, checking in existing files to create new versions is still allowed.
[1955] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open an application where you want to create the file (e.g., Word, PowerPoint).
[1956] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Enter your content and click ⟦B⟧Save⟦/B⟧.
[1957] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click the ⟦B⟧File⟦/B⟧ tab at the top.
[1958] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to the ⟦B⟧Save As⟦/B⟧ tab and click ⟦B⟧Browse⟦/B⟧.
[1959] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In the ⟦B⟧Save As⟦/B⟧ window, select Wrapsody Drive for desktop, select a subfolder under Company, Group, Personal, or Shared drive where you have Write permission, then click ⟦B⟧Save⟦/B⟧.
[1960] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Save result
[1961] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       The file is saved in the specified folder within Wrapsody Drive. The user who saved the file is designated as the owner. File permissions are inherited from the folder permissions: users with Write permission for the folder are granted Revise permission, and users with Read permissions are granted View permission.
[1962] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Copy files in Wrapsody Drive (Create Branch file)
[1963] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When a file is copied within Wrapsody Drive or from an external path into Wrapsody Drive, a new Branch file is created and saved with the same filename but a different Sync ID. Files for which you have View permission or higher (or Revise permission or higher, depending on the server settings) can be copied to folders where you have Write permission.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Since files with the same Sync ID cannot exist in multiple locations within Wrapsody Drive, a new Branch is created during the copy process.
[1964] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[1965] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive (W:)⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧, or go to a path outside Wrapsody Drive on your PC.
[1966] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click the desired file and select ⟦B⟧Copy⟦/B⟧, or click the file and press Ctrl + C.
[1967] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Move to another folder within Wrapsody Drive.
[1968] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: If you copied a file from Wrapsody Drive, you can also move to a folder path in another drive.
[1969] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click an empty area and select ⟦B⟧Paste⟦/B⟧, or press Ctrl + V.
[1970] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Refer to the illustration below for the result of copying a file in Wrapsody Drive.
[1971] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦D0⟧
[1972] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Copy result
[1973] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive ⟦/B⟧>⟦B⟧ Local path⟦/B⟧: A file with the same Sync ID is saved, retaining the same file usage permissions.
[1974] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Local path ⟦/B⟧>⟦B⟧ Wrapsody Drive⟦/B⟧ or ⟦B⟧Within Wrapsody Drive⟦/B⟧: A new Branch file under the same filename but with a different Sync ID is created. The user who performs the copy action becomes the owner, and all previous user permissions are reset. Permissions are then inherited from the destination folder: users with Write permission for the folder are granted Revise permission, and users with Read permission are granted View permission.
[1975] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Plain files remain as plain files after being copied or are encrypted according to the Wrapping policy.
[1976] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Move files in Wrapsody Drive
[1977] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can move files within Wrapsody Drive for which you have Revise permission to folders for which you have Write permission, or move them from Wrapsody Drive to your local path. Moving files within Wrapsody Drive is available only within the same Company, Group, Personal Drive, or shared folders, and the Sync ID remains unchanged after the move. Individually assigned user permissions are retained, while folder permissions are inherited at the same time: users with Write permission for the folder are granted Revise permission, and users with Read permission are granted View permission.
[1978] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Notes⟦/B⟧
[1979] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can’t move files between top-level shared folders in the Shared Drive.
[1980] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Moving Wrapsody files between Wrapsody Drive and a local path is not supported. Files are copied instead of being moved. However, plain files in a local path can be moved to Wrapsody Drive.
[1981] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[1982] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive (W:)⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧.
[1983] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click the desired file and select ⟦B⟧Cut⟦/B⟧, or click the file and press Ctrl + X.
[1984] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Move to another folder within Wrapsody Drive.
[1985] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: If you copied a file from Wrapsody Drive, you can also move to a folder path in another drive.

       Right-click an empty area and select ⟦B⟧Paste⟦/B⟧, or press Ctrl + V.

[1990] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0

       Delete files in Wrapsody Drive (delete from Wrapsody server)
[2006] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       You can delete files in folders for which you have Write permission. Whether deleted from Wrapsody Drive for desktop or Wrapsody Drive Web, files are also deleted from the Wrapsody server. Deleted files in Wrapsody Drive are moved to the owner’s ⟦H0⟧Trash in Wrapsody web⟦/H0⟧.
[2007] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: If you accidently delete a file owned by another user, you can ⟦H0⟧restore it from the desktop⟦/H0⟧.

[2020] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Restore files in Wrapsody Drive
[2021] heading=0 drawings=0 links=2 trailing_lb=0
       Deleted files in Wrapsody Drive can be ⟦H0⟧restored either from Trash of the owner⟦/H0⟧ or directly within Wrapsody Drive. Whether the file is restored from Wrapsody Drive for desktop or Wrapsody Drive Web, it is removed from ⟦H1⟧Trash in Wrapsody web⟦/H1⟧ and returned to its original location.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Files cannot be restored after the retention period expires.

       Create folders in Wrapsody Drive
[2037] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can create folders in Company, Group, Personal, and Shared Drives. In Company and Group Drives, subfolders can be created only within folders for which the user has Write permission. The user who creates a folder becomes its folder manager, and the folder’s permissions are inherited from its parent folder.

[2058] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Copy result
[2059] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive ⟦/B⟧>⟦B⟧ Local path⟦/B⟧: A folder with the same name is copied. Files within the folder are saved with the same Sync ID as in Wrapsody Drive, retaining the same file usage permissions.
[2060] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Local path ⟦/B⟧>⟦B⟧ Wrapsody Drive⟦/B⟧ or ⟦B⟧Within Wrapsody Drive⟦/B⟧: The user who performs the copy action becomes the folder manager, and the folder inherits the permissions of the destination path. For files within the folder, a new Branch file is created and saved with the same filename but a different Sync ID. The user who performs the copy action becomes the owner of the files, and permissions are inherited from the destination folder: users with Write permission are granted Revise permission, and users with Read permission are granted View permission.
[2061] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Within Wrapsody Drive⟦/B⟧: The user who performs the copy action becomes the folder manager, and the folder inherits the permissions of the destination path. Individually assigned folder permissions are not retained. For files within the folder, a new Branch file is created with the same filename but a different Sync ID. The user who performs the copy action becomes the owner of the files, all previous user permissions are reset, and permissions are inherited from the destination folder: users with Write permission for the folder are granted Revise permission, and users with Read permission are granted View permission.
[2062] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Move folders in Wrapsody Drive
[2063] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can move folders for which you have Write permission to folders for which you also have Write permission. However, when moving folders within Wrapsody Drive, the move is only allowed within the same Company, Group, or Personal Drive, or within a shared folder.

       Share folders in Wrapsody Drive
[2138] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A folder manager can share folders in Personal or Group Drives with other users or groups. Shared folders appear in the ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧ section, and users can view or edit files according to the permissions granted. Depending on internal settings, the folder-sharing feature may not be supported.
[2139] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Notes
[2140] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       The folder-sharing feature may not be supported depending on internal settings.

[2344] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Key features of Virtual Drive
[2345] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Virtual Drive is a virtual drive in Wrapsody that enables users to manage files efficiently within a familiar folder structure. Files do not inherit permissions from their folders, allowing independent permission management for each file.
[2346] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Virtual Drive is available in two versions: a web version, accessible through Wrapsody on the web, and a desktop version, accessible from the file explorer on your PC. Both versions stay synchronized in real time, ensuring that the latest files are always available wherever you access them.
[2347] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Virtual Drive overview
[2348] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Depending on the Virtual Drive management policy, Personal, Group, or Company Drive may not be displayed.
[2349] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Personal Drive⟦/B⟧: A personal workspace for the logged-in user. It is displayed in the format [User name (User ID)] (e.g., Kim Fasoo (fasoo.kim)).
[2350] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Group Drive⟦/B⟧: A workspace for the group or to which the logged-in user belongs. It is displayed under the team or group name. All members of the group can access the Group Drive folder, but access to subfolders depends on each user’s individual permissions.
[2351] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Company Drive⟦/B⟧: A workspace for managing organization-wide files. All members of the organization can access the Company Drive folder, but access to its subfolders depends on each user’s individual permissions.
[2352] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧: A workspace that contains folders shared with the logged-in user. All shared folders the user has access to are displayed here.
[2353] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧My Group⟦/B⟧: When the logged-in user is a direct manager or holds a higher-level permission, they are granted view permission for folders of their managed groups. Even folders without permission can be viewed through the ⟦B⟧My Group⟦/B⟧ drive. In addition, the user can request edit permission for subgroup folders if needed.
[2354] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Access Virtual Drive
[2355] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can access and use Virtual Drive files both on the web and on your desktop.
[2356] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0

[2363] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Company, Group, and Personal Drives in Virtual Drive have storage limits. You can check the storage limit for each drive and the amount of space currently in use.

[2370] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Desktop
[2371] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your desktop, you can check only the Storage information of Company, Group, or Personal Drive.
[2372] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[2373] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Virtual Drive (V:)⟦/B⟧.
[2374] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Personal Drive⟦/B⟧.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: The drive management feature is not available for subfolders under Personal, Group, or Company Drive.
[2375] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody ⟦/B⟧> ⟦B⟧Drive Properties⟦/B⟧. The ⟦B⟧Details⟦/B⟧ window of the drive appears.
[2376] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Refer to the descriptions below for each item.
[2377] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧ · ⟦B⟧Group ⟦/B⟧· ⟦B⟧Personal Drive Storage⟦/B⟧: Displays capacity information, including the space allocated to the selected drive and the space currently in use (the total size of the latest versions of all files). It also shows the total size of all versions of all files.
[2378] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Total⟦/B⟧: Displays the storage limit assigned to the drive.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: When ⟦B⟧Total⟦/B⟧ displays ⟦B⟧Unlimited⟦/B⟧, which does not have limit, data for other items is not displayed.
[2379] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Used⟦/B⟧: Displays the amount of space currently occupied by the drive, calculated as the total size of the latest versions of all files.
[2380] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Free⟦/B⟧: Displays the remaining storage space.
[2381] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Total capacity of all file versions⟦/B⟧: Displays the combined size of all versions of all files in the drive.
[2382] heading=0 drawings=2 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Daily storage usage⟦/B⟧: Displays the daily storage usage of the selected drive in a graph. You can click the bar chart⟦D0⟧ or line chart⟦D1⟧ to view the data in the desired graph type. You can also select a specific period during which drive activity occurred to view data for that period at a glance.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: This data is available only on the web.
[2383] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Top 50 files with the largest sizes (Latest version only)⟦/B⟧: Lists the top 50 files in the selected drive with the largest latest-version sizes.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: The ⟦B⟧Top 50 files with the largest sizes (Latest version only)⟦/B⟧ list is displayed only to users who have ownership of the selected drive. For heads of groups, the list appears in Group Drive, while for group members, it appears only in Personal Drive. This data is available only on the web.

[2410] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Manually sync all files in folder in Virtual Drive for desktop
[2411] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Virtual Drive for desktop automatically synchronizes with the Wrapsody server in real time, ensuring files are always up to date. Additionally, you can manually synchronize files in the desired path.
[2412] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[2413] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Virtual Drive (V:)⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧.
[2414] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click a file in the drive, then select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Synchronize All Files In Same Folder⟦/B⟧.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Alternatively, click a folder, then select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Synchronize All Subfolders and File⟦/B⟧.
[2415] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       All files in the folder synchronize.
[2416] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Convert files in Virtual Drive for desktop to link files
[2417] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In Virtual Drive for desktop, you can store files by converting them to link files. Link files occupy zero memory space and function as shortcuts, distinguished by a green overlay mark⟦D0⟧ at the bottom left of the icon.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: To convert a link file back into an original file that occupies storage space, open the file.
[2418] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       On your PC, open ⟦B⟧File Explorer⟦/B⟧.
[2419] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Wrapsody Drive (W:)⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧.
[2420] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click on a file in the drive and select ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧ > ⟦B⟧Convert to Link File⟦/B⟧. The file is converted to a link file, marked with the green overlay mark at the bottom left of the icon.
[2421] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Manage files and folders in Virtual Drive
[2422] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Creating, copying, moving, or deleting folders or files in Virtual Drive works in the same way as it does for folders or files on your PC.
[2423] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Wrapsody Drive Web and Wrapsody Drive for desktop are synchronized in real time, ensuring you can access the latest files from any path.
[2424] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When a file or folder is modified in Shared Drive, the same changes are synchronized with the original file or folder in Personal or Group Drives.
[2425] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Remove files in Virtual Drive
[2426] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Files located in folders for which you have Write permission or higher can be removed from the path regardless of your file-level permissions. In the case of Virtual Drive files, deleting them from Virtual Drive for desktop or Virtual Drive Web removes them from the path, but the files still remain on the Wrapsody server.
[2427] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Depending on internal settings, you may also be able to remove folders for which you have Read permission or higher.
[2428] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Web

       ⟦H0⟧Go to Wrapsody on the web⟦/H0⟧.

[2431] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to the ⟦B⟧Company⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Group⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Personal⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧ tab.
[2432] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In the desired path, hover over a file, click More⟦D0⟧, then click ⟦B⟧Remove⟦/B⟧.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Alternatively, in the desired path, hover one or more files, select the checkboxes, then click ⟦B⟧Remove⟦/B⟧ at the top.
[2433] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       In the ⟦B⟧Delete File⟦/B⟧ confirmation window, click ⟦B⟧Delete⟦/B⟧. The files disappear from the path.

       Right-click a folder you want to rename, then click ⟦B⟧Rename⟦/B⟧.
[2514] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Enter the new name and press Enter. The folder name is updated.
[2515] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Share folders in Virtual Drive
[2516] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A folder manager can share folders in Personal or Group Drives with other users or groups. Shared folders appear in the ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧ section, and users can access files according to the permissions granted. Since files in Virtual Drive do not inherit permissions from their parent folders, the permissions of folders and files are managed separately.
[2517] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Notes
[2518] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       The folder-sharing feature may not be supported depending on internal settings.
[2519] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Shared folders are displayed in the following formats:
[2520] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Shared from Personal Drive⟦LB⟧[Original folder name] - [User name (ID)]
[2521] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Shared from Group Drive:⟦LB⟧[Original folder name] - [Group or team name]_[User name (ID)]
[2522] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       To share a subfolder within a shared folder, configure sharing from the original drive, not from ⟦B⟧Shared Drive⟦/B⟧.

[2666] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A folder manager can modify user permissions for a folder at any time. Since files in Wrapsody Drive do not inherit permissions from their parent folders, each file’s permissions can be managed separately from folder access control.

[2675] heading=0 drawings=3 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Grant permission⟦/B⟧: In the organization chart on the left, click Add⟦D0⟧ next to the desired user or group. If the target already has permission, clicking the button removes them from the list. Click the dropdown⟦D1⟧ next to the target and select the permission to grant (⟦B⟧Read⟦/B⟧ or ⟦B⟧Write⟦/B⟧).⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Granting permissions to a group does not automatically apply them to its subgroups. To grant permissions to subgroups, you must add them manually. If a subgroup does not have permissions, a crown is displayed on its group icon (⟦D2⟧).

[2886] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Refer to the descriptions below for each item.
[2887] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Revised⟦/B⟧
[2888] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Total: Total number of check-ins completed by all users in the organization
[2889] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Average: Total check-ins divided by the total number of users
[2890] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Viewed⟦/B⟧
[2891] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       View count includes every instance of opening a file regardless of mode (check-out, view, or preview).
[2892] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Total: Total number of views by all users in the organization
[2893] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Average: Total views divided by the total number of users
[2894] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Engaged (Inbound)⟦/B⟧
[2895] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Total: Sum of views per user for files that were checked in within the server-defined period (default: 3 days).
[2896] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Average: Total engagement (Inbound) divided by the total number of users
[2897] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Engaged (Outbound)⟦/B⟧
[2898] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Total: Total number of users who were granted View or Revise permission for files that were checked in within the server-defined period (default: 3 days)
[2899] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Average: Total engagement (Outbound) divided by the total number of users
[2900] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Usage Trend⟦/B⟧
[2901] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Displays a graph visualizing the organization’s daily totals for ⟦B⟧Revised⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Viewed⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Engaged (Inbound)⟦/B⟧, and ⟦B⟧Engagement (Outbound)⟦/B⟧. The data reflects the period selected in the ⟦B⟧Period⟦/B⟧ filter. If you click an item at the top, that item becomes inactive and its data is no longer displayed on the graph.

[2975] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧If the same file exists⟦/B⟧: If you select ⟦B⟧Original location⟦/B⟧ in ⟦B⟧Restore documents in⟦/B⟧, select how to handle the same files when an original file still exists in that location during the restore process. If you do not need to back up the existing file, select ⟦B⟧Overwrite⟦/B⟧ to replace the file currently in that location with the restored file. If you select ⟦B⟧Move the original files to⟦/B⟧, click Select path⟦D0⟧ and specify the path, all existing files will be moved to the specified location. If you select ⟦B⟧Add ‘.BAK’ to the original filename⟦/B⟧, the existing file will be renamed with “.BAK,” and the restored file will be placed in the original location.

       Under ⟦B⟧Storage server list⟦/B⟧, a list of available storage servers is displayed.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Clicking ⟦B⟧Measure Speed⟦/B⟧ displays the current speed of each server.
[3084] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Refer to the descriptions below for each item.
[3085] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Server name⟦/B⟧: Displays the name of the server.
[3086] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Server address (IP)⟦/B⟧: Displays the address of the server.
[3087] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Speed⟦/B⟧: Displays the most recently measured speed.
[3088] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Status⟦/B⟧: Displays ⟦B⟧Connected⟦/B⟧ if you are currently connected to the server. Click ⟦B⟧Connect ⟦/B⟧to switch to that server.
[3089] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Connect to another storage server
[3090] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧Show hidden icons⟦/B⟧⟦D0⟧ on the right side of the taskbar.
[3091] heading=0 drawings=2 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Right-click ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧⟦D0⟧, then select ⟦B⟧Settings⟦/B⟧. The ⟦B⟧Wrapsody File Manager - Settings⟦/B⟧ window appears.⟦LB⟧⟦B⟧Note⟦/B⟧: Alternatively, right-click ⟦B⟧Wrapsody⟦/B⟧⟦D1⟧, then select ⟦B⟧Open Wrapsody File Manager⟦/B⟧. Click the ⟦B⟧Settings ⟦/B⟧tab in the left side bar.
[3092] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Go to ⟦B⟧Storage Management⟦/B⟧ tab.
[3093] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Under ⟦B⟧Storage server list⟦/B⟧, a list of available storage servers is displayed. In the ⟦B⟧Notes⟦/B⟧ column of the server you want to connect to, click ⟦B⟧Connect⟦/B⟧. The ⟦B⟧Change Current Storage Server⟦/B⟧ confirmation window appears.
[3094] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Click ⟦B⟧OK⟦/B⟧. You are connected to the selected server.

[3124] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Troubleshooting
[3125] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Emergency recovery of the Wrapsody client
[3126] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       If you encounter issues while using Wrapsody, you can ⟦H0⟧restore the software using the Emergency Recovery app⟦/H0⟧.
[3127] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       FAQ
[3128] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Troubleshoot document management issues
[3129] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: Why are Branch files created automatically even though I never created one myself?
[3130] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A: Branch files may be created automatically in the following exceptional situations, even if you did not create them manually:
[3131] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When a user without sufficient permission edits a file and saves it
[3132] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When a user opens a file in View mode while another user has already checked it out, then edits and saves it
[3133] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When a user edits a file offline and reconnects while another user checked in a newer version
[3134] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       When the application closes unexpectedly or a system error occurs
[3135] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Automatic Branch file creation is designed to preserve your changes safely in conflict situations. Checking your permission level and Revise mode before editing can help reduce unnecessary Branch file creation.
[3136] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: Why do I see a popup asking me to rename the file every time I open a specific file?
[3137] heading=0 drawings=0 links=2 trailing_lb=0
       A: This message appears when the filename stored on the server is different from the filename stored on your PC. You can resolve this by renaming the local file (⟦H0⟧Rename local files⟦/H0⟧) or by renaming the server file (⟦H1⟧Rename server files⟦/H1⟧).
[3138] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       However, note that if you rename the server filename, all users who have a local copy of the file will also receive a “Change Local Filename” message.
[3139] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: I used the Export Original feature to convert a Wrapsody file into a plain file, but when I open it again, it gets wrapped.
[3140] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A: This occurs because an automatic Wrapping policy is applied to the target path. Check with your Wrapsody administrator to see if there is an exception path for automatic Wrapping. If so, save the exported file to that exception path to keep it as a plain (unwrapped) file.
[3141] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Check out, edit, and check in
[3142] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: What is the difference between “Save” and “Check In”?
[3143] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A: ⟦B⟧Save⟦/B⟧ (or Ctrl+S) stores the file locally on your PC. The changes are not uploaded to the Wrapsody server and are not shared with other users. In contrast, ⟦B⟧Check In⟦/B⟧ uploads your changes to the Wrapsody server and registers them as a new version. The history of file changes is recorded in Timeline, and users with permission can view it. However, note that a check-in may occur automatically after saving, depending on your environment settings or organizational policy.
[3144] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: I want to edit a file, but I’m seeing a message saying that another user has checked it out.
[3145] heading=0 drawings=0 links=3 trailing_lb=0
       A: This message indicates that another user has checked out the file. You can send an ⟦H0⟧End Editing request⟦/H0⟧ to the user who has checked out the file. After another user checks it in, ⟦H1⟧update the file⟦/H1⟧ and start editing. Alternatively, you can ⟦H2⟧create a Branch file⟦/H2⟧, which allows you to edit independently without affecting the original file.
[3146] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: Can I view who has currently checked out a file?
[3147] heading=0 drawings=4 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A: Yes, you can. If you are viewing the file on your PC, click More⟦D0⟧ at the top right, then check the user information displayed next to the red check-out icon⟦D1⟧. From Wrapsody web or Wrapsody File Manager, locate the file and hover over the check-out icon⟦D2⟧ next to the filename to see who has checked it out. You can also click Details⟦D3⟧ to open the file info window and check the ⟦B⟧Checked out by⟦/B⟧ field.
[3148] heading=1 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Use Wrapsody Drive
[3149] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: What is the difference between wrapping a file on my PC to create a Wrapsody file and creating a file directly in Wrapsody Drive?
[3150] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       A: When you wrap a file on your PC to create a Wrapsody file, you create and manage the file locally, and you must configure permissions individually for each file. In contrast, when you create a file in Wrapsody Drive, you can manage it based on the folder structure of Wrapsody Drive. Any permissions configured for a folder are automatically applied to all files within that folder, making permission management much simpler. Wrapsody Drive also synchronizes with the server in real time, ensuring that you can always access the latest version of your files from anywhere. For example, if you rename a file locally, the filename on the server is automatically updated as well.
[3151] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Q: How are Revise · View permissions different from Write · Read permissions?
[3152] heading=0 drawings=0 links=1 trailing_lb=0
       A: Revise and View permissions apply to individual files, while Write and Read permissions apply to folders. If you have Write permission for a folder, you automatically receive Revise permission for the files in that folder. If you have Read permission for a folder, you receive View permission for the files. For more details on how permissions work for folders and files within Wrapsody Drive, refer to ⟦H0⟧Rules for granting permissions in Wrapsody Drive files⟦/H0⟧.

[3543] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Filename⟦/B⟧: Displays the name of the file registered on the Wrapsody server.
[3544] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Owner⟦/B⟧: Displays the user who has ownership of the file.
[3545] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Deleted/Restored by⟦/B⟧: Displays the user who deleted or restored the file, or approved its permanent deletion.
[3546] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Status⟦/B⟧: Displays the type of deletion, such as ⟦B⟧Move to Recycle Bin (Delete)⟦/B⟧, ⟦B⟧Restore⟦/B⟧, or ⟦B⟧Permanent Delete⟦/B⟧.
[3547] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Date deleted/restored⟦/B⟧: Displays the date and time when the file was deleted, restored, or permanently deleted.
[3548] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       Filters
[3549] heading=0 drawings=1 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Filename⟦/B⟧: Searches for the usage history of files whose names contain the entered keyword. Type a keyword and press Enter, or click Add⟦D0⟧.
[3550] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Deleted/Restored by⟦/B⟧: Searches for the history of files deleted, restored, or permanently deleted by a specific user. When you type a keyword, a dropdown list appears showing Wrapsody users whose names or IDs include the entered text. You can select the desired user, but cannot add users who do not exist.
[3551] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Last revised⟦/B⟧: Searches for the history of files that were last checked in at a specific date and time.
[3552] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Reset⟦/B⟧:⟦B⟧ ⟦/B⟧Clears all applied filter conditions when clicked.
[3553] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Set as current version⟦/B⟧
[3554] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       You can view the history of versions that were set as the current version.

[3558] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Registered version⟦/B⟧: Displays the version number after being set as the current version.
[3559] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Copied by⟦/B⟧: Displays the user who set the version as the current version.
[3560] heading=0 drawings=0 links=0 trailing_lb=0
       ⟦B⟧Date copied⟦/B⟧: Displays the date and time when the version was set as the current version.
